subject: Discovery recap: tool/function calling + structured output (next steps)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma@saascorp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Discovery recap: tool/function calling + structured output (next steps)

Thanks for the call today — great to meet you and the team. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Pain points / goals
- Primary pain: customer-facing automation frequently returns free-form text that is difficult to parse reliably; you need deterministic JSON responses for downstream systems.
- Tool invocation concerns: current system does ad-hoc tool calls to payment and CRM APIs with inconsistent error handling and retry semantics.
- Success criteria: consistent JSON schema adherence (no extra fields), deterministic ordering for a subset of fields, idempotent tool calls with clear failure semantics, and <200ms median response for the majority of interactive flows.

Current stack
- In-house LLM-based assistant + homegrown orchestrator; runs on GCP; lightweight caching but no persistent KV for agent state.

Redwood proposal highlights (high-level)
- Structured output enforcement: schema-first generation with validation layers and deterministic serialization options.
- Tool/function calling: managed tool adapters with retry/backoff, explicit call logs, and a sandbox mode for dry-run testing.
- Agent workflows: step-by-step orchestration with checkpointing and KV caching to avoid repeated external calls.

Immediate next steps
1) We're attaching a provisional JSON schema (provisional_json_schema.json) — please confirm this matches the shape you expect or flag required fields.
2) Dev (cc'd) will send a sample agent workflow + an initial deterministic-serialization checklist.
3) Schedule a technical deep dive (30–45m) with your engineering leads — proposed window: Feb 23 or Feb 24 (US morning/PT).
4) If procurement needs a ballpark SOW, we can provide a one-page scope and timing after the tech dive.

Open questions
- Which fields must be strictly ordered vs. can be alphabetized?
- Any existing schema validation/tech we should integrate with (e.g., JSON Schema drafts, custom validators)?
- Do you need signed audit logs and retention controls for every tool call (regulatory requirement)?

Thanks — we want to make the POC as low-friction as possible. Please reply with preferred time for the tech deep dive and any schema edits.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | (555) 555-0123
From: Emma Johnson <emma@saascorp.com>

Date: 2026-02-18T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: tool/function calling + structured output (next steps)

Thanks, Jordan — helpful summary and aligned on the priorities.

A few clarifications:
- Deterministic formatting is mission-critical for us; we can't tolerate schema drift. The ordered fields are: transaction_id, customer_id, action, timestamp, result. Everything else can be unordered.
- Procurement note: we'll need a rough cost estimate and example SLA for the POC before Mar 5 to expedite internal approval.
- Security: we will want SOC2 evidence and an option for encrypted logs at rest (KMS). I'll loop in procurement separately (procurement@saascorp.com).

I've attached our internal requirements doc (requirements_v1.docx) — it has a sample payload and a brief list of approval gates.

Proposed time for tech deep dive: Feb 23, 10:00am PT works for our eng lead.

—

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-02-18T17:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: tool/function calling + structured output (next steps)

Hi Emma — thanks for the quick response and the attachment. A few technical notes ahead of the Feb 23 deep dive:

- Attached: json_schema_v1.json (initial mapping based on today's call) and agent_workflow_sketch.drawio (high-level orchestrator steps).
- Deterministic output: Redwood supports a "schema-first" generation mode where we enforce required fields and provide a deterministic serializer. For fields you flagged as strictly ordered we can emit an ordered object (we'll serialize to a canonical form) and run schema validation before any external tool call.
- Tool invocation semantics: we recommend a two-phase call pattern for side-effectful tools — 1) dry-run/validate step returning a signed intent blob, 2) execute step that references the intent blob. This provides idempotency and auditability.
- Performance: For the POC we can target median 150–180ms for single-tool calls in dedicated mode; we will size a small Dedicated pool for predictable latency during the evaluation window.

Next steps I will take before the Feb 23 call:
- Update the schema with the exact ordered fields you listed.
- Provide a short checklist for deterministic serialization success criteria (how we'll test it with your payloads).
- Draft a one-page POC scope & ballpark pricing for procurement.

If anyone needs alternative times Feb 23, flag them here. I'll send calendar invites once Jordan confirms.

—
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
